A couple weeks ago, my wife and i were outside trying to catch some of the perseid meteor shower. We were lucky enough to see some amazing shooting stars, however we also noticed many "stars" that were moving perfectly along a plane.

They were much smaller and way higher than any aircraft, with no visible lights. We saw 3 each night we went out, and 4 on the final night. Could it of been satellites, or space junk moving in orbit? I am curious as to what else they could be? Any thoughts?
Is it possible to see satellites moving with the naked eye?

That sounds like satellites to me, and I've seen plenty. If you know where to look, you can usually spot a couple on any given night. There are a few sites out there that show which ones you can see. I've always used Heavens-Above.

It probably wasn't the ISS, because that's usually a lot brighter. On a good pass, it's about as bright as Venus, and brighter than any star.

Now, you can usually only see satellites for 2-3 hours after sunset and the same time before sunrise. If the ones you saw were in the middle of the night, then I dunno.
Indeed they were in the middle of the night. I'd say from 10pm to 11pm est
This time of year, that's pretty much the perfect time to see them. By "middle of the night", I meant more like 1AM, since sunset for me is around 8:30.

Yep. Just get somewhere dark enough and at the right time (far enough after sunset it is dark, but close enough the sun can still illuminate the low orbit satellites) and you can see plenty of them. One night in the mountains above Yosemite I gave up counting how many there were.

They basically look like a bright small star, flashing (if it's rotating) and moving along at a jet-speed clip until they enter Earth's shadow and wink out.

There are websites and apps that tell you when/where to look for them.
That is a perfect description of what we saw.
